title: Tenma Tsukasa — Lessons With Kikyogumi〔Part2〕Side Story (Part 2)

rows.Line: Morinomiya Music Academy - Rehearsal Room

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Hmm...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
You're here already, Tsukasa?
Are you practicing by yourself?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
I was, but...
I'm having a little trouble with something...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Remember how our last lesson involved males playing female characters?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: They taught us how to stand and walk, but I simply can't get my body to do what I want...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: After all, it's because you're acting while also focusing on aspects of your bearing you've never had to think about before.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: They say that onnagata actors in the world of kabuki live their daily lives with feminine mannerisms. For them, it may hardly fall under acting at all.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: It's certainly not something we can pick up in one day.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: You say that, but you seemed to do pretty well back there.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: The others were astonished by how quickly you improved over the course of one day.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Hehe. The truth is, I've watched video footage of an all-male ballet company put on a performance a number of times.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I wasn't expecting the analysis I performed of their physical expression to come back and help me like this.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: It just goes to show that it's important to keep your eyes open for anything and everything one can use.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Oh, I didn't know that...!
Would it be possible for me to also watch that video?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
I don't know...
It was a stream that I just happened to stumble across, but I can try looking for it.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Anyway, are you done practicing?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
No...
Nothing will come of me running circles in my head!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: So, let's review what we covered during our last lesson!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Do you have time to watch what I do for a bit, Rui?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, that's the plan.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: (Starting with my shoulders. They still feel too square...)

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Grrr! Why is this so hard...?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I can't seem to lower my shoulders without slouching. And every time I try to walk with my knees closer together, I end up waddling instead.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, I may be your friend, but I must say that you make for a wonderful penguin.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
Yes, I'm well aware of that!
How can you laugh at me like that?! I'm trying my best over here!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line:
I know.
Let me apologize by telling you a trick I learned while practicing on my own. Will that suffice?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Oh? Let's hear it.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: In order to make your shoulders look more round, try to make it as if your wrists are pulling them down.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Hm? My wrists?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: The person who showed me was apparently told to not slouch, and to relax his shoulders more, as part of an assignment in order to improve his acting.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Thus, the key is to not curl your shoulders, but to drop them instead. That's supposed to prevent you from slouching.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: And to avoid putting too much focus on his shoulders, he envisioned his wrists, far below his shoulders, pulling his arms down.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I should also mention that he said, “It's a solution I arrived on for this problem, so I can't say that it's for everyone...”

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: No, I believe his reasoning is sound.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: It's difficult not to slouch when you're trying to round your shoulders...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: But you have to concentrate quite a lot in order to push them down, which ends up affecting everything else you do.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: In order to prevent that, you need to drop them instead of trying to round them. That's where your wrists play a key role...

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: So, am I right to say that this helps?

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Yes! Now I'm glad that I got you to laugh at my waddling!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: So, let me try this again, using the method you just described! Tell me what you think!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line:
How's this, Rui?!
This should look much better compared to before!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, you're using your upper body much better now! Your posture has also improved, and you look much less like a penguin now.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Excellent! To think that one trick would end up helping this much!

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Still, that's incredible...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: What you learned didn't come from a teacher, but another student, yes? He really came up with this all on his own?

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, because he knew this was a problem for him. He apparently struggled quite a lot before arriving upon this solution.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: I see...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: We're all doing our best to improve by correcting our mistakes...

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: But this fellow's efforts deserve more recognition.

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: I suppose that's what it means to be a student at Morinomiya.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: As I thought, we stand to learn a tremendous amount by taking lessons here!

rows.Speaker: Rui
rows.Line: Yes, we do. We need to make the most of the three months we have with them.

rows.Speaker: Tsukasa
rows.Line: Agreed!
